transcript:
Header: 2025-07-28 11:00 AM PT / 15:00 UTC — Duration 46m
Attendees: Ava Thompson (Redwood AE), Marcus Lee (Redwood SE), Dr. Rina Patel (Satellite Health CTO), Carlos Mendez (Sr ML Eng), Lena Ortiz (Head of Product)
Recording link: https://app.fireflies.ai/recordings/fh-20250728-5462 (note: placeholder)

[00:00] Ava: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Ava, Redwood AE, and with me is Marcus, our SE. Appreciate you making time. Quick intro then we'll go into your goals.
[00:20] Rina: Thanks, Ava. I'm Rina, CTO at Satellite Health. We're ingesting patient messages and want an LLM layer for summarization and triage — HIPAA scope so, so that's the big ask. Quick question — how fast can we get to first token with your hosted API, and what's included in free credits?
[00:40] Ava: Great question. For self-serve hosted, teams typically hit first token within an hour — sign up, API key, run the quickstart. We include starter credits for new sign-ups; I'll send the exact credit link after. The quickstart includes a sample call, SDK snippets, and a recommended prompt template.
[01:05] Carlos: When you say "first token in an hour" — do you mean fully instrumented with SSO and logging? Or just raw API access? Our security team needs an audit trail.
[01:18] Ava: Good clarification. First token is raw API access plus basic usage logs in the console. For SSO/SAML, VPC, and enterprise audit retention you move into Dedicated or Private which takes longer to provision — usually a few weeks for Dedicated with reserved capacity.
[01:35] Marcus: To add, for secure logs and KMS integration that's part of the Private/Dedicated enterprise stacks. Hosted can egress logs but if you need customer-managed keys or specific retention windows, we recommend Dedicated or Private.
[01:50] Lena: So we could start on hosted to iterate product and then migrate? How seamless is that?
[02:00] Marcus: Yes, that's the common path. Same API surface — you can pin model versions and swap routing rules without changing client code. The big changes are in networking (VPC) and key management. We provide a migration checklist.
[02:20] Rina: Our workload: roughly 12k patient messages per day, average prompt length ~150 tokens, we want triage classification and a 1-2 sentence summary. Latency target is pretty tight — ideally under 250ms p95 for the short path. Cost must be predictable. Thoughts?
[02:45] Marcus: 12k/day at 150 tokens is modest, but latency p95 under 250ms is aggressive depending on model choice and batching. On hosted, you can use smaller open models we curate with lower tail latency; Dedicated gives you reserved capacity and lower jitter. We also have prefix caching for repeated prompts which helps.
[03:05] Carlos: What about KV cache — will that help with long patient histories? We don't want repeated rehits to be expensive.
[03:15] Marcus: Yes, KV cache (sometimes auto transcribed as KV cash) stores past tokens for faster next-token generation and reduces compute for repeated contexts. Caching needs deterministic session keys for PHI handling; with Dedicated/Private you can configure cache eviction and retention.
[03:30] Rina: HIPAA — can Redwood sign BAA?
[03:36] Ava: Short answer: yes, we do BAA for enterprise Private and Dedicated customers. For hosted, we have a BAA program for qualifying customers under certain controls — we'll share legal and security docs.
[03:50] Lena: What about data residency? We need data to stay in US regions only.
[03:56] Marcus: We support region routing; Dedicated and Private let you pin inference to specific cloud regions. Hosted generally has regional endpoints in US/EU/APAC but you'd want Dedicated to guarantee isolation.
[04:10] Carlos: Any customers using Redwood for PHI now?
[04:14] Ava: Yes, a few health-tech customers run on Dedicated with BAAs. I'll send references and an anonymized case study.
[04:25] Rina: On the performance side — how do you size Dedicated? If we wanted to guarantee 200ms p95 for our 150-token prompts and 200 qps at peak, what's the ballpark?
[04:40] Marcus: Ballpark depends on model and GPU type. For smaller quantized open models on A100-class, 200 qps with low tail latency might be a couple of dedicated nodes with continuous batching. We'll propose a sizing after we see your prompts and run a micro-benchmark.
[04:58] Carlos: Are there auto-scale or burst options? We have spikes (end of day messaging) and can't overprovision constantly.
[05:06] Marcus: Dedicated supports configurable autoscaling with burst capacity. You can set burst policies and soft failover back to hosted if dedicated capacity is full. That said, mixing modes requires careful routing rules.
[05:23] Rina: Security — SAML SSO, RBAC, and audit logs are must-haves. How granular is RBAC?
[05:30] Ava: RBAC supports team-level roles, route-level permissions, and token management. Audit logs include token-level usage and model version inferences; for extended retention we offer add-on retention packages.
[05:46] Lena: Pricing question: how do you recommend we think about cost vs latency tradeoffs — for example, cheaper quantized models vs more expensive higher quality models?
[05:58] Marcus: It's workload dependent. For triage classification, smaller models often suffice. For nuanced clinical summarization you might need a higher-capacity model. Redwood Optimize gives model/quantization recommendations per prompt set; we'll run a quality-vs-cost sweep in the benchmark.
[06:20] Carlos: We ran internally against OpenAI and saw good quality but cost was high. Any guidance on interpolation?
[06:27] Marcus: We'll compare open models we host with Anthropic / OpenAI baselines and show token cost and latency tradeoffs. Often you can combine — generate classification with a small model and escalate to a stronger model for edge cases.
[06:40] Rina: Can we see observability — per-route latency, token costs per prompt, and tracing?
[06:47] Ava: Yes, Redwood Console has per-route dashboards, token-level cost breakdown, and traces. We'll include a screenshot in the docs we send.
[06:58] Lena: Onboarding flow — what's the path to a pilot? We want to test inference quality on a week-long pilot with ~50k messages.
[07:08] Ava: Typical pilot: sign-up with free credits to run local evals, then a 2-week dedicated pilot with reserved capacity for realistic load and a single benchmark run with Marcus. We'll map success criteria and an acceptance test.
[07:22] Carlos: About PHI — is there client-side encryption for inputs at rest?
[07:28] Marcus: For Private and Dedicated, yes: customer-managed KMS and optional encryption at rest with customer keys. Hosted has encrypted-at-rest with provider-managed keys unless you opt-in to enterprise key options.
[07:40] Rina: We need to run some regulatory review. Can you share SOC2, ISO, pen-test reports?
[07:46] Ava: Absolutely — will attach security pack and contact info for our security team.
[07:52] Lena: Any gotchas moving from hosted to private on networking? We are behind a strict corporate firewall.
[07:58] Marcus: Private is usually deployed in the customer's VPC or on-prem stack; that avoids the firewall issue. Dedicated can also be put into a private VPC peering setup. We'll document the network diagrams.
[08:12] Rina: On risk — if we start on hosted and then need to migrate because of compliance, what's the rollback plan?
[08:20] Ava: We typically stage routes: start traffic on hosted with a canary to dedicated/private. Because the API surface is identical, it's an operational switch: change route policy and pin a model/version. There's a checklist for data egress, KMS, and session token rotation.
[08:36] Carlos: Can we run a small benchmark this week? I can share a redacted dataset.
[08:42] Marcus: Yes, if you share samples we'll run a micro-benchmark against a couple of candidate models and return latency/cost/quality matrices.
[08:50] Rina: What's the usual timeline for the pilot? We want something before mid-August.
[08:56] Ava: If you share data by July 31, we can schedule the benchmark the week of Aug 4 and aim for a pilot mid-August.
[09:05] Lena: Any governance for prompt logging — we log prompts for audit, but need controls to purge PHI.
[09:12] Marcus: We support redaction tooling and retention policies on logs. For stricter needs you can route logs to your own S3 with lifecycle rules.
[09:22] Carlos: Regarding SDKs — do you have official Python and Node? We use a Python stack.
[09:26] Ava: Yes, official SDKs for Python/Node/Go. We also have Kubernetes examples for Dedicated and Helm charts for private deployments.
[09:36] Rina: Pricing again — are there minimums for Dedicated?
[09:40] Ava: Dedicated reserves capacity, so there are commit levels — monthly or annual. We'll include sample pricing tiers in the docs. For pilots, we can do short-term reserved trials.
[09:51] Carlos: I saw mention of "continuous batching" in your docs — can you explain briefly?
[09:56] Marcus: Continuous batching aggregates requests on the GPU to increase throughput without adding much latency; it's workload-aware. It helps lower per-token cost while meeting latency SLOs. We'll show charts in the benchmark.
[10:12] Lena: Anything else we should know for the pilot success criteria?
[10:16] Rina: For me, success is: (1) quality at or above internal OpenAI baselines for 90% of cases, (2) p95 latency under 300ms for short prompts, (3) proof of secure handling of PHI and ability to sign BAA.
[10:30] Ava: Great — we'll map to a one-pager acceptance criteria and add to next steps.
[10:36] Marcus: I'll draft a benchmark plan: models to test, metrics, and a rough Dedicated sizing.
[10:42] Carlos: Are there any limitations on model fine-tuning or RLHF in your stack? We may want to tune prompts or do a small fine-tune.
[10:50] Marcus: We support fine-tuning workflows for certain model families; we'll check licensing and model compatibility. For many customers, prompt engineering and few-shot pipelines suffice.
[11:00] Ava: Ok quick recap: Ava will send quickstart + credits + security pack; Carlos will share redacted sample messages and target metrics; Marcus will prepare benchmark plan and propose Dedicated sizing. Schedule technical deep dive for next week.
[11:18] Rina: Sounds good, thanks.
[11:22] Ava: Thanks all, we'll follow up with calendar invites.

Notes about transcript quality: automated transcription occasionally mislabels acronyms (VPC->V-P-C) and technical terms (KV cache -> KV cash). Natural speech artifacts present (uh, um, overlaps).

References and shared artifacts mentioned:

End of meeting.
